title: Impersonal se: who was forced to work

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6 (*se trabaja mucho aquí*): the verb stays singular when there is no noun to agree with. With a person after *a*, it works the same way: *se obligaba a los indígenas a trabajar*. It leaves out who did the forcing, which suits the history of forced labour.

sections.title: Singular verb, person with a
rows: Se obligaba a los indígenas a trabajar.
singular verb *obligaba* even though *indígenas* is plural
Se enviaba a los hombres a las minas.
no noun at all: singular verb

items.spanish: Se obligaba a los indígenas a trabajar en las minas.
items.english: The indigenous people were forced to work in the mines.

items.spanish: Cada año se enviaba a un grupo de hombres a las minas de Potosí.
items.english: Every year a group of men was sent to the mines of Potosí.

items.spanish: Se trabajaba por turnos, y se pagaba un salario bajo.
items.english: People worked in shifts, and a low wage was paid.

items.spanish: En la práctica se seguía obligando a muchos indígenas a trabajar.
items.english: In practice many indigenous people were still being forced to work.

sections.content: When *se* comes with a person introduced by *a*, the verb does not change: *se obligaba a los indígenas*, not *se obligaban*. Compare *se buscan personas* from B1 Unit 6, where the verb agrees with a noun.
